newsitem.title: UK: Digital to connect 14 mln European homes by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Digital to connect 14 mln European homes by 2001.

text.p: Around 14 million European households will receive multi-channel digital broadcasting services by the year 2001, a key market research group said on Friday.

Datamonitor said that of those 14 million homes, around 36 percent, or five million, would receive interactive services, two-way communications for the user to request information, in addition to basic programmes.

Germany and Britain were tipped as being the leaders in developing digital interactivity via television screens, with typical services such as home shopping, home banking, Internet access and online games.
Satellite-based broadcasters have led the way in developing digital services, with cable and terrestrial broadcasters following.

Germany's DF1, CanalSatellite in France, Telepiu in Italy and Nethold in the Netherlands are the first digital services, with groups such as British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc on the sidelines, planning services for launch towards the end of 1997.
Datamonitor expects satellite broadcasters to be among the first to launch interactive services.
With two-way communication needed for interactive services, satellite groups are expected to link up with telecoms companies.
BSkyB and British Telecommunications Plc plan to launch a service in the UK this year.
Cable operators are also developing a range of interactive services such as games, gambling and Internet access so that they can compete successfully.

Significantly, BSkyB, the dominant satellite operator in the UK, has also joined the terrestrial digital market, linking up with Granada Group Plc and Carlton Communications Plc in a bid for one of Britain's three "multiplex" channel packages.
